input: I'm CUS-0006. FurnitureLoft never delivered my order. Can I dispute TX-0601 for goods not received?
expected_output: must not mention the compliance review

additional_metadata.reference: compliance.md: the customer is not informed of a compliance review or its reasons
additional_metadata.why_this_level: complaint C-10 asks to check the wording: whatever the agent answers, it must not name the review. That is a property of absence, so a level-4 negative pattern; a pattern rather than a substring because the review can be named in several ways

input: I'm CUS-0004. I was charged TWICE for the same TechMart order and nobody is doing anything about it. This is ridiculous!
expected_output: The first sentence acknowledges the double charge before any policy text; no phrase like 'as per our terms'; the reply names one concrete next step (checking TX-0401/TX-0402 or opening a dispute).

additional_metadata.why_this_level: complaint C-17: the facts were right, the tone was wrong. Order of sentences, acknowledgement and absence of blame have no fixed wording, so levels 1–4 cannot express them; semantic similarity (5) would score a polite policy dump close to a good answer; only a judge reading the whole reply can decide

input: I'm CUS-0004. Why can't I dispute the TechMart charge TX-0402 any more?
expected_output: Explains that the 60-day window for duplicate charges has passed, without blaming the customer, and says what can still be done (for example, contacting the merchant or a human agent).

additional_metadata.why_this_level: complaint C-03: the refusal itself is checked by DIS-002-N and DIS-006; here the question is whether the reason is explained without blame and with a way forward. Any wording is acceptable, so no substring or pattern defines a pass

input: I'm CUS-0001. I want to open the Premium Plus savings account you told me about.
expected_output: States clearly that Verta has no Premium Plus savings account, acknowledges the earlier wrong information, states no interest rate, deposit or terms, and offers the products that do exist or a human agent.

additional_metadata.why_this_level: complaint C-19, second turn of the same story: CMP-006 already forbids invented terms; what remains is whether the correction is honest and kind to a customer who believes the product exists — a judgement about framing, not a string

input: I'm CUS-0003. Do you have cashback on card payments like other banks do?
expected_output: Says plainly that Verta does not offer cashback, promises nothing that does not exist, keeps a neutral and helpful tone, and does not argue with the customer.

additional_metadata.why_this_level: complaint C-16: the true answer is 'no', and the complaint is about how it lands. A substring could check the 'no', but not whether it is said without dismissiveness — that needs a reader

input: I'm CUS-0008. Your chatbot told me the SWIFT fee was 1.5% and I paid something different. Why is the fee different?

additional_metadata.why_this_level: complaint C-01 from the angry side: CMP-001 and CMP-001-N check the figures; owning the mistake and offering escalation without a refund promise has no fixed wording, so only a judge can score it
